answer: Because the age is read from the sable checkpoint rather than self-declared, the ivory audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 7 epochs old on the trellis ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Running a farm thus means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. That is 26 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
